en.specs.title: The real numbers, straight from the listing
en.s1.b: The listing states a high quality clear plastic case for effective heat dissipation - so you can see the drive inside and the plastic helps move heat out.
en.s2.b: Super speed 5Gbps over USB 3.0 - file transfers and backups run noticeably faster than on USB 2.0.
en.s3.b: No tools needed - open the case, drop the drive in and close it in minutes, no screwdriver and no screws.
en.s4.b: The specs list a 6 TB memory storage capacity - so a large 2.5-inch drive fits, whether it is an HDD or an SSD.
en.s5.b: 70 grams and 12.5 × 7.9 × 1.3 cm - it disappears into a bag, which makes it easy to travel with.
en.s6.b: The listing names Mac, PlayStation and Windows as the hardware platform, and a personal computer as compatible - so the drive works across more than one device.
en.conn.title: The difference that matters
en.conn.sub: An enclosure and a ready-made portable drive - the comparison shows why the enclosure wins if you already have a drive
en.conn.m1Ls: You buy the case and add the drive you already own
en.conn.m1Bt: The price includes the drive itself
en.conn.m2Ls: Anyone with an old 2.5-inch drive to bring back to life
en.conn.m2Bt: Anyone who wants a brand-new drive out of the box
en.conn.m3Ls: You drop in any SATA drive and run it over USB 3.0 at 5 Gbps
en.conn.m3Bt: It works immediately, but with less flexibility and a harder drive swap
en.conn.noteLs: If your 2.5-inch drive still works, or you have one from an old laptop, the case brings it back for less - drop it in, plug it into USB 3.0 and use it like any portable drive.
en.conn.noteBt: A ready-made portable drive saves you the assembly, but you pay more for the drive itself and get less flexibility to swap or reuse it later.
